speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I see you have double vision, trouble climbing stairs, and upper limb weakness; to determine the cause of these symptoms, have you noticed any trouble swallowing or breathing difficulties?

speaker: Patient
text: The double vision usually happens when I look up or down, and the weakness in my arms and legs gets worse after activity but improves if I rest. I have not noticed balance problems or numbness.

speaker: Doctor
text: That pattern of worsening weakness with activity and improvement with rest is classic for myasthenia gravis, especially combined with your eye symptoms; do you have a history of drooping eyelids or difficulty swallowing food or liquids?

speaker: Patient
text: I have not had recent infections or fevers, and there is no family history of neurological disease. The weakness feels symmetrical in both arms and legs.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Myasthenia Gravis. The combination of fluctuating weakness worsening with activity, improvement with rest, and specific ocular involvement (double vision) is diagnostic. I am requesting an Acetylcholine Receptor Antibody test to confirm.
